summary: The S. 323, PLAN for Broadband Act requires the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to create and implement a national strategy to better coordinate federal broadband programs and agency evaluations of broadband infrastructure applications on federal land. It requires executive branch agencies to track and address processing delays for communication use applications, establishes staff alerts for applications at risk of missing the 270-day deadline, and lowers the project cost threshold for certain broadband infrastructure projects to qualify for expedited environmental review under the FAST Act.

affected_groups.effect: Must participate in developing the national strategy, coordinate programs, adopt common data sets and application rules, and submit implementation reports.
Must track processing times, analyze delay factors, issue annual reports, and set up employee alerts for applications nearing the 270-day review deadline.
affected_groups.group: Executive agencies reviewing communications use applications

affected_groups.effect: Projects involving broadband infrastructure with investments over $5 million that are subject to NEPA may qualify for expedited federal environmental reviews under the FAST Act.

key_provisions: Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to develop and submit a National Strategy to Synchronize Federal Broadband Programs within one year of enactment.
Requires the Assistant Secretary to develop and publish a public implementation plan for the strategy within 120 days of its submission, including a minimum 60-day public comment period.
Requires covered executive agencies to report on their progress in coordinating with NTIA and the FCC to populate the Deployment Locations Map.

Mandates that executive agencies develop data controls, analyze and report on delay factors, and establish employee alert methods for applications at risk of missing the 270-day review deadline for communications use applications.
Amends the FAST Act to lower the cost threshold for certain broadband infrastructure projects subject to NEPA to qualify for expedited federal environmental review from $200 million to $5 million.
missing_information: Exact funding amounts or appropriations authorized to carry out the strategy and implementation plan are not specified.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The S. 323, PLAN for Broadband Act requires the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to create and implement a national strategy to better coordinate federal broadband programs and agency evaluations of broadband infrastructure applications on federal land. It requires executive branch agencies to track and address processing delays for communication use applications, establishes staff alerts for applications at risk of missing the 270-day deadline, and lowers the project cost threshold for certain broadband infrastructure projects to qualify for expedited environmental review under the FAST Act.
summary_detail.significance: The bill addresses federal broadband coordination, application processing delays on federal property, and environmental review thresholds for broadband projects. The significance score reflects a moderate structural and administrative change across multiple federal agencies involved in broadband deployment.
